free_tier.stated: A Small Compute application can request "up to and including 1,000,000 CPU or GPU SBU (standard billing units) of cluster computing on Snellius Supercomputer", "Up to and including 500,000 CPU core-hours and/or 14,000 GPU hours of cluster computing on the LUMI pre-exascale supercomputer", "up to and including 1,000,000 CPU core hours or 10,000 GPU hours of Data Processing on Grid and/or Spider", and "up to and including 50,000 CPU core hours or 5,000 GPU hours of cloud computing on HPC Cloud via SURF Research Cloud", with a maximum duration of one year.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: This is the largest set of numbers in the file reachable without a competitive review: 14,000 LUMI GPU-hours plus 500,000 LUMI core-hours plus a million SBU on Snellius, decided on technical feasibility in about two weeks. It composes badly with nothing except the Dutch contract, which is the whole gate.

limits.value: Eligibility is a tenured or tenure-track appointment at a Dutch university, university of applied sciences, university medical centre, KNAW or NWO institute, and a temporary appointment qualifies only if the employer guarantees the project's completion, so the 14,000 LUMI GPU-hours are unreachable without a Dutch contract.

evidence.proved: up to 1,000,000 CPU or GPU SBU on Snellius; up to 500,000 CPU core-hours and/or 14,000 GPU hours on LUMI; up to 1,000,000 CPU core hours or 10,000 GPU hours of data processing; up to 50,000 CPU core hours or 5,000 GPU hours of HPC Cloud, quoted

"researchers must have either a tenured appointment [...] or a tenure track appointment at one of the research organisations listed below"; for small applications a temporary appointment qualifies only if the organisation "guarantees the computing time project's duration and completion", quoted
"Affiliates of one of the Dutch Universities or Grand Technology Institutes can submit an application for compute resources through NWO", quoted
"A researcher may submit a maximum of one computing time application per compute facility per calendar year directly to SURF"; maximum duration one year, quoted
"These requests will only be assessed on technical feasibility by SURF and are usually handled within 2 weeks", quoted

notes: Two properties make this the most interesting refutation. The review is not a merit panel but a feasibility check, so the allocation is closer to an administrative entitlement than to INCITE or EuroHPC; and the LUMI portion is a second, separate door into a machine the corpus already records under lumi.json as requiring a consortium country's Resource Allocator, which is a different and slower route than NWO Small Compute. The corpus holds no SURF or NWO record. SBU on Snellius is a billing unit whose ratio to core-hours the page does not state, so the Snellius figure is left as SBU rather than converted.
